io.milvus.common.utils

Class RoaringBitmapUtils

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.milvus.common.utils.RoaringBitmapUtils

  • public class RoaringBitmapUtils
extends Object
    Builds a client-side roaring bitmap blob for the roaring_match(field, {blob}) filter expression.

    Where BloomFilterUtils trades exactness for size, this is the exact-membership sibling: roaring_match never produces a false positive, and a dense integer set compresses far better than a bloom filter of the same set — one million consecutive ids is a 274-byte blob here versus roughly 2 MB as a bloom filter at a 0.005 false-positive rate. Sparse random sets are the other way round, so pick per workload: a roaring blob's size follows the value distribution, not the member count. Pass the result through filterTemplateValues; it travels as a native protobuf bytes value with no base64 inflation, and the server embeds it verbatim after validating the envelope. 

    
 byte[] blob = RoaringBitmapUtils.buildRoaringBitmap(userIds);
 QueryReq req = QueryReq.builder()
         .collectionName("docs")
         .filter("roaring_match(user_id, {ids})")
         .filterTemplateValues(Collections.singletonMap("ids", blob))
         .build();

    Members are signed integers only, and the target field must be an integer field (or an integer-valued JSON path). A member is sign-extended to int64 and its two's-complement bit pattern is reinterpreted as the unsigned bitmap key, so an INT8 -1 and a long -1 land on the same key 0xffffffffffffffff and produce the same blob. All ordering inside the bitmap is on that unsigned key, which is why {-1, 5} is stored as {5, 0xffffffffffffffff}.

    Building a large bitmap is the expensive part of a roaring_match query, so the returned array is meant to be built once and reused across many requests rather than rebuilt per call.

    The body is the standard portable Roaring64 serialization (the same one CRoaring's portable format and the Go roaring/v2 library's WriteTo emit), wrapped in the Milvus MRB1 envelope. Blobs built here are byte-identical to the ones the Go SDK (roaringfilter.Build) produces for the same members — the golden vectors in src/test/resources/roaring/roaring_golden_vectors.json are generated from it and pin that. The other SDKs are held to the same vectors as their support lands. See docs/design-docs/design_docs/20260714-roaring-exact-membership-expression.md in the milvus repository.

        public static final int MAX_DECODED_BYTES
        Maximum estimated decoded size the server accepts, mirroring its own admission check. The estimate is body_length + 128 * high_containers + 64 * low_containers: the wire body plus the per-container bookkeeping the server allocates when it decodes.

    • Method Detail

      • buildRoaringBitmap

        public static byte[] buildRoaringBitmap(List<? extends Number> members)
        Builds a bitmap over the given members.

        Members must be Byte/Short/Integer/Long; each is sign-extended to int64. Duplicates and unsorted input are fine — the same set always produces the same bytes. An empty list produces a valid 40-byte blob that matches nothing.

        Parameters:
        members - the membership set
        Returns:
        the MRB1 blob to pass as a filter template value
        Throws:
        MilvusClientException - if members is null, contains a null or a non-integer element, or the resulting bitmap exceeds a server limit
